notes.typography: Curly apostrophes and quotes are intentional. Keep them when building.
notes.ai: AI is not mentioned anywhere on the page, by choice. Nothing on the page needs it.
notes.f4Sub: film.f4.sub is empty on purpose. The four panel lines are the reading on this screen, each one answering a note from f3. A sub here would be a fifth thing to read while the panels light up, and every draft of it restated the ongoing promise outside its three placements (hero, f5, picker).
notes.stepLabels: The third label is “From then on”, not “Every week”. Posting is weekly, but website changes, review replies and fresh ads happen when something changes, and no weekly ad cadence is confirmed.
notes.ads: Ads copy says we make and run them. “Facebook, Instagram and Google” is the owner-speak for Meta and Google placements. “Your own ad money” says who pays without stating a budget or amount.
notes.workIntro: Removed on 2026-09-18 at Karan's request ("Remove the small paragraph right next to this section"). It read: "These are in-house examples. Real projects take their place as soon as a client says we can show them." The page's disclosure now rests only on footer.honestyNote.
notes.contactHint: Removed on 2026-09-18 at Karan's request, together with the rule that sat under it (the details row's top border). It read: "Whichever you check between services"

sub.why: Karan's copy (2026-09-18). He sent it with an em dash; the deck forbids dash characters, so the question mark closes the clause and a full stop follows. Option 1 is what was live until then and carried the audience line; with this one the hero no longer names the audience, which now sits in the footer and the meta description.

charge.why: Karan, 2026-09-19: "an icon in the front that will have scroll text right next to it. The more I scroll, the icon fills up, and when it is fully filled up, it then kind of slingshots into the air". The word beside the charge icon in the slingshot cloud beats. picker.intro: Pick the one that sounds like your week. You’ll see our plan, and the form below fills itself in.
picker.empty: Nothing picked yet. The steps build here, from the first fix up.

steps.first: We open your site on a phone, the way a hungry stranger would, and note everything that gets in the way.
steps.then: We fix it or rebuild it around what people come for: menu, directions and booking, up top.
steps.everyWeek: When a dish changes, we change the site and your Google listing with it.

steps.first: We fix your Google listing: menu link, phone number, your photos and the category you’re filed under.
steps.then: We make the site quick to load and write it around what locals type, like “brunch near me”.
steps.everyWeek: We answer every new review, good or bad, and keep the listing in step with the site.

steps.first: We use your photos, even a quick phone shot of the special, and design the post when there isn’t one.
steps.then: We write captions with the dish names off your menu board, so posts sound like your place, not a chain.
steps.everyWeek: We post every week, each post tied to what’s on, like the soup coming back for winter.

steps.first: We pick the one thing each ad should sell, like a set lunch or a night you want busier.
steps.then: We make the ads and run them on Facebook, Instagram and Google, using your own ad money.
steps.everyWeek: We swap the ads when what’s on changes, so nobody sees an ad for last month’s special.

steps.first: We look at your website, Google listing, posts and ads together, and start where it’s worst.
steps.then: We fix that, then bring the other three into line so they all say the same thing.
steps.everyWeek: You give us access once. After that, the posts, ads, listing changes and review replies are ours.

steps.first: You tell us what is going wrong, in your own words, on the phone or in the form below.
steps.then: We look at your site, Google listing, posts and ads together, and say plainly what we would do.
steps.everyWeek: We take on the part you hand over and keep it running every week, the way the rest of this list works.
